body:
Fiery Maw
CR 4

The floating ball of fire stops, sensing your presence, a large toothed maw forming as it lunges forward.

XP 9,600
N Medium outsider (elemental, extraplanar, fire)
Init +1; Senses low-light vision; Perception +5

DEFENSE

AC 16, touch 11, flat-footed 15 (+1 Dex, +5 natural)
hp 34 (4d10+12)
Fort +6, Ref +7, Will +1
Immune elemental traits, fire; Weakness vulnerability to cold

OFFENSE

Speed fly 40 ft. (perfect)
Melee bite +7 (1d8+3 plus burn)
Special Attacks burn (1d6, DC 15), explode (DC 15)

STATISTICS

Str 16, Dex 13, Con 16, Int 4, Wis 10, Cha 10
Base Attack +4; CMB +7, CMD 18 (cannot be tripped)
Feats Ability Focus (explode), Improved Natural Attack (bite)
Skills Fly +6, Perception +5
Languages ignan

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Burn (Ex)

A fiery maw deals fire damage in addition to damage dealt on a successful bite. Those affected by the burn ability must also succeed on a Reflex save or catch fire, taking the listed damage for an additional 1d4 rounds at the start of its turn. A burning creature can attempt a new save as a full-round action.

Dropping and rolling on the ground grants a +4 bonus on this save. Creatures that hit a burning creature with natural weapons or unarmed attacks take fire damage as though hit by the burning creature and must make a Reflex save to avoid catching on fire.

Explode (Ex)

When reduced to 10 hit points or lower, a fiery maw will explode with a concussive fiery explosion as a standard action. All creatures within 20 feet take 4d6 fire damage. A DC 16 Reflex save halves this damage. After the explosion, the fiery maw is destroyed. The damage increases by 1d6 for each HD the fiery maw possesses and the save DC is Constitution-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment any (plane of fire)
Organization solitary, duo, or blister (3-6)
Treasure none

A fiery maw is a derivation of fire elementals that resemble a roiling ball of fire with a gaping mouth full of flaming teeth. They enjoy setting and spreading fires, and if nearly defeated, will explode in a last ditch attempt to spread their fires, knowing they will simply be returned to the plane of fire.
